title: U.S. House · Ohio's 2nd District
area: Southwestern Ohio, including parts of the Cincinnati suburbs and southeastern Ohio counties

context.text: The Cook Political Report rates the 2nd District R+21, one of the more strongly Republican-leaning seats in Ohio's 2026 map.

candidates.name: David Taylor
candidates.ballotNote: Incumbent; defeated Bob Carr in the May 5, 2026 Republican primary, 75.0% to 25.0%

summary.text: David Taylor is the Republican incumbent for Ohio's 2nd District, an Ohio native who worked as an attorney in the Clermont County Prosecutor's Office and later as president of his family's business before winning the open seat in 2024. He serves on the Agriculture and Transportation and Infrastructure committees and is seeking a second term.

background.text: Born in Ohio in 1969; attended Amelia High School, according to his congressional biography.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Miami University in 1992 and a law degree from the University of Dayton School of Law.
Joined the Clermont County Prosecutor's Office after law school, where his congressional biography says he tried criminal cases.
Returned to work for his family's business, Sardinia Ready Mix, Inc., where he served as president, according to his congressional biography and Ballotpedia.
Won the open 2nd District seat in November 2024 (73.6% in the general election), succeeding Brad Wenstrup, and took office January 3, 2025.

Serves on the House Agriculture and Transportation and Infrastructure committees, where he is vice chairman of the Water Resources and Environment Subcommittee. Co-chairs the bipartisan Congressional Rural Broadband Caucus.
Lives in Clermont County with his wife, Charity; they have three daughters, according to his congressional biography.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Agriculture (Commodity Markets, Digital Assets and Rural Development; General Farm Commodities, Risk Management and Credit) and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure (Highways and Transit; Railroads, Pipelines and Hazardous Materials; Water Resources and Environment) in the 119th Congress.

candidates.name: Jen Mazzuckelli
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary, 53.3% to 46.7%, over Todd Wilson

summary.text: Jen Mazzuckelli is the Democratic nominee, a former human-resources professional and high school English teacher. She describes her campaign as centered on congressional oversight of the executive branch and responsiveness to constituents, drawing on her experience with economic hardship.

background.text: Describes growing up in a middle-class family of public servants; her mother was a teacher and her father retired from the Public Health Service.
Graduated from Glen Este High School in Clermont County, Ohio, and attended Trinity College in Washington, D.C., before earning a bachelor's degree from Illinois College (1991).
Earned a graduate degree from Miami University of Ohio (2005).
Worked in human resources, then became a licensed teacher and taught high school English until 2013.

Says her life changed in 2013 with a domestic-violence case against her husband and a multiple sclerosis diagnosis, after which her family fell to an "extremely low" income level; she cites that experience as a reason for running.
Describes community service as a Girl Scout leader and assistant coach for Girls on the Run.

priorities.text: Says Congress needs a representative who 'genuinely listens to our concerns and is responsive to OUR needs' and 'acts as a public servant NOT a politician,' criticizing incumbent David Taylor for refusing in-person town halls.
priorities.quote: We need a representative who genuinely listens to our concerns and is responsive to OUR needs. We need a representative that acts as a public servant NOT a politician.

priorities.text: Says a key responsibility of Congress is oversight of the executive branch, including scrutinizing spending and released frozen or impounded appropriations.
